title: Audit Logging and Regulated Release Evidence

scout.purpose: Master audit logging and regulated release evidence through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend audit logging and regulated release evidence.

blocks.text: Audit logs answer who or what authority performed which protected action, on which object, under what policy, with what outcome and correlation. They differ from debug logs and analytics. The trusted service usually creates the authoritative record because the client can be modified, offline, or replayed. Use stable event types, server time, actor and delegated authority, operation ID, result, reason category, policy or configuration version, and evidence link without copying sensitive payloads.

blocks.text: Tamper evidence can use append-only storage, restricted writers, integrity controls, signed exports, or chained records according to risk; no mechanism makes a bad event truthful. Protect access, separation of duties, retention, legal hold, deletion exceptions, residency, and incident use. Clock skew, retries, offline actions, batch imports, administrator impersonation, and redaction need explicit semantics. Correlation IDs must not become credentials. Users may need transparency or export without exposure of internal fraud rules.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Regulated release evidence maps requirement to control, implementation, test, artifact, reviewer, result, exception, owner, and expiry. Preserve source revision, signed binary digest, dependencies, SBOM, mappings and symbols, test and security reports, approvals, configuration, migration, monitoring, rollout, rollback, and incident readiness. Evidence should be reproducible, access-controlled, and version-specific—not screenshots assembled after release. Rehearse an audit query and recall drill.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

blocks.title: Expert trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Writing audit records only from the Android client lets a modified or offline client omit, forge, reorder, or replay authoritative actions.

inspect.title: Inspect Audit Logging and Regulated Release Evidence
walkthrough: Identify the user or platform outcome, authority, lifecycle, supported versions, and exact artifact context.
Trace data, execution, security, compatibility, delivery, and failure ownership across every boundary.
Verify representative evidence, adverse paths, release gates, support, migration, and safe recovery.
inspect.expectedOutput: A reproducible expert artifact or investigation with explicit contracts, limitations, evidence, and operational ownership.

trap_check.mistake: Writing audit records only from the Android client lets a modified or offline client omit, forge, reorder, or replay authoritative actions.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Design an end-to-end audit trail and release evidence pack for a regulated payment change, including access, retention, exceptions, approvals, recall, and reconstruction.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.answer: It is bound to exact source, configuration, artifact, tools, tests, reviewers, outcomes, and retained raw records.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
